title: Crypto-Asset Regulation and Supervision
summary: An advanced twelve-module programme equipping supervisors to authorise, supervise and take action against crypto-asset firms under comprehensive regimes and international standards.
intro: This training programme equips supervisory staff to authorise, supervise and take action against crypto-asset service providers and issuers under a comprehensive crypto-asset regime, applying international standards with structured, evidence-based judgement.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To equip supervisors with the practical tools to apply a comprehensive crypto-asset regime across the full supervisory lifecycle, from authorisation and risk-based supervision to enforcement and crisis management. Participants leave able to test business models, governance, prudential resources, custody and financial crime controls, and to look beneath firms' documentation to how they actually operate.
sections.What It Covers: The crypto-asset ecosystem, international standards and comprehensive crypto-asset regimes, service provider business models, governance and internal controls, prudential resources, authorisation, risk-based supervision, custody and operational resilience, market abuse, AML/CFT and sanctions, stablecoins and systemic risk, and cross-border cooperation, enforcement and crisis management.
Intended Audience: Supervisors and authorisation staff responsible for crypto-asset service providers and stablecoin issuers
Risk, prudential, enforcement and financial crime specialists covering digital finance
Senior managers responsible for the authority's crypto-asset supervisory strategy
Learning Objectives: Explain the international standards for crypto-assets and how comprehensive regimes apply them to issuers and service providers
Assess business models, governance, internal controls and prudential resources of crypto-asset firms
Evaluate authorisation applications and operate a risk-based approach to ongoing supervision and inspection
Assess custody, safeguarding and operational resilience arrangements for crypto-asset operations
Evaluate market abuse, money laundering, terrorist financing and sanctions risks and the controls firms use to manage them
Apply supervisory, enforcement and crisis management tools, including cross-border cooperation and stablecoin oversight
sections.Structure and Format: Twelve modules of about four hours each, grouped into five pathways and delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, as a multi-week programme or as a series of half-day sessions with pre-reading. Each module combines a technical briefing with case studies, red-flag exercises and practical supervisory tools, and pathways or individual modules can be selected or tailored to the authority's regime.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Completion of Crypto and Blockchain Fundamentals, or equivalent experience of crypto-asset markets, is helpful. Some experience of authorisation, supervision or enforcement work is recommended but not mandatory.
Core Reading: FSB, High-level Recommendations for the Regulation, Supervision and Oversight of Crypto-Asset Activities and Markets (2023)
FSB, High-level Recommendations for the Regulation, Supervision and Oversight of Global Stablecoin Arrangements (2023)
IOSCO, Policy Recommendations for Crypto and Digital Asset Markets (2023)
FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers (2021)

modules.title: The Crypto-Asset Ecosystem for Supervisors
modules.summary: A supervisor's map of the technology, assets and market structure of the crypto ecosystem, focusing on where control really sits, how value and risk flow, and where failures typically originate.
objectives: Explain how distributed ledgers, tokens and crypto-asset markets operate in practice
Identify the true control points, incentives and accountability gaps in the ecosystem
Analyse the technical and operational failure modes that drive consumer and prudential harm
syllabus: Public, permissioned and hybrid ledgers: design choices and supervisory leverage
Issuers, validators, venues, custodians, market makers and end users
Control points: upgrades, forks, admin keys, oracles and listings
Failure modes: smart contract flaws, oracle manipulation and off-chain dependencies

modules.title: International Standards and Comprehensive Crypto-Asset Regimes
modules.summary: The international standards for crypto-assets and how comprehensive regimes translate them into perimeter, authorisation, conduct, prudential and disclosure requirements, including where gaps and ambiguities create supervisory risk.
objectives: Explain the objectives and content of the main international crypto-asset standards
Analyse how comprehensive regimes classify crypto-assets, issuers and service providers
Evaluate gaps between formal compliance documentation and actual firm behaviour
syllabus: FSB high-level recommendations and global stablecoin recommendations
IOSCO crypto and DeFi policy recommendations; FATF Recommendation 15
Basel Committee standard on banks' crypto-asset exposures
Regime architecture: primary law, technical standards, guidance and white papers

modules.title: Business Models of Crypto-Asset Service Providers
modules.summary: The business models of issuers, exchanges, brokers, custodians and infrastructure providers across the centralised-to-decentralised spectrum, and how supervisors use business model analysis to locate risk.
objectives: Differentiate centralised and decentralised models and where regulatory obligations attach
Map common business models to regulated services and their prudential and conduct risks
Apply business model analysis to test viability, conflicts and substance
syllabus: The centralised-to-decentralised spectrum and perimeter questions
Conflicts of interest: exchanges as market makers, lenders and custodians
Red flags: opaque fees, proprietary tokens and fragmented group structures
Stress-testing projections, organisation charts and outsourcing registers

modules.title: Governance, Risk Management and Internal Controls
modules.summary: How to look beneath a crypto firm's governance documents to judge whether its management body, risk, compliance and audit functions are genuinely effective, and how to intervene proportionately.
objectives: Assess the composition and functioning of the management body and its oversight functions
Evaluate the independence, resourcing and influence of risk, compliance and internal audit
Apply proportionate supervisory interventions to governance and control weaknesses
syllabus: Board composition, fitness and propriety and founder-dominated governance
Three lines of defence and risk appetite in a crypto business
Red flags: governance capture, nominal independence and marginalised control functions
Intervention tools: management requirements and independent expert reviews

modules.title: Prudential Risk, Financial Resources and Sustainability
modules.summary: How capital, liquidity and wind-down requirements apply to crypto-asset service providers and issuers, and how supervisors identify financially fragile firms before problems become critical.
objectives: Apply capital and liquidity requirements to different service provider and issuer types
Evaluate liquidity mismatches, contingency funding and recovery planning
Identify prudential red flags and select appropriate supervisory responses
syllabus: Own funds, liquidity and wind-down planning for service providers
Revenue volatility, market cycles and reliance on affiliate funding
Red flags: thin capital, related-party exposures and untested projections
Prudential returns analysis, stress testing and early warning indicators

modules.title: Authorising Crypto-Asset Service Providers
modules.summary: A proportionate, risk-based framework for assessing applications from crypto-asset service providers, testing substance, governance, group dependencies and operations before authorisation is granted.
objectives: Operate an authorisation gateway with clear quality thresholds and early challenge
Assess application dossiers systematically, from programme of operations to ICT security
Evaluate substance, group dependencies and conflicts to prevent letter-box authorisations
syllabus: Completeness, quality thresholds and risk-based prioritisation of applications
Programme of operations, business plans, management and shareholder suitability
Group structures, intragroup outsourcing and local substance
Regulatory history, customer journeys and exposure to unregulated or DeFi services

modules.title: Risk-Based Supervision in Practice
modules.summary: How to design and run a risk-based supervisory approach to crypto firms: prioritising resources, monitoring between engagements, conducting inspections and using graduated powers to drive remediation.
objectives: Design a risk-based framework that allocates resources by impact and probability
Conduct ongoing monitoring using returns, market intelligence and early warning indicators
Plan, execute and follow up inspections of crypto-asset firms
syllabus: Firm risk assessment, supervisory planning and resource allocation
Red flags triggering enhanced engagement: rapid growth, turnover and incidents
Inspection methodology: document requests, interviews and walkthroughs
Graduated supervisory powers and tracking remediation

modules.title: Custody, Safeguarding and Operational Resilience
modules.summary: How crypto custody and the wider ICT estate work in practice, the operational, cyber and third-party risks they create, and how supervisors verify that client assets and critical services are protected.
objectives: Explain custody architectures, including cold storage, hardware security modules, multi-signature and MPC
Assess safeguarding, segregation and reconciliation of client assets
Evaluate ICT risk management, incident reporting and third-party dependencies
syllabus: Proprietary custody, third-party custodians and sub-custody chains
Red flags: commingling, weak key controls and missing independent reconciliation
Cloud concentration, API dependencies and on-chain/off-chain integration risk
Incident reporting, resilience testing and exit planning for critical providers

modules.title: Preventing Crypto Market Abuse
modules.summary: How insider dealing and manipulation occur in crypto markets, from wash trading to maximal extractable value, and how supervisors assess surveillance and use suspicious order reports as intelligence.
objectives: Identify insider dealing and unlawful disclosure risks in token issuance and trading
Detect traditional and crypto-native manipulation schemes
Assess firms' trade surveillance and suspicious transaction and order reporting
syllabus: Market abuse prohibitions adapted to crypto-asset markets
Wash trading, spoofing, pump-and-dump schemes and MEV exploitation
Surveillance systems, alert calibration and investigation workflows
Investigative techniques: order book analysis and on-chain tracing

modules.title: AML/CFT, the Travel Rule and Sanctions
modules.summary: The money laundering, terrorist financing and sanctions evasion typologies seen in crypto markets, and how supervisors test firms' controls and coordinate findings with the national FIU.
objectives: Identify illicit finance and sanctions evasion typologies specific to crypto-assets
Evaluate customer due diligence, transaction monitoring, travel rule and screening controls
Apply AML/CFT supervisory techniques and coordinate with the national FIU
syllabus: Typologies: mixers, privacy coins, cross-chain hopping and high-risk exchanges
Blockchain analytics: capabilities, limits and use as a verification tool
FATF travel rule in practice: unhosted wallets and the sunrise issue
Red flags, wallet screening and the role of the money laundering reporting officer

modules.title: Stablecoins and Systemic Risk
modules.summary: How stablecoins are structured and supervised, the reserve, redemption and governance risks that determine whether a peg holds, and how stress can transmit to the wider financial system.
objectives: Distinguish stablecoin structures and how design drives risk and regulatory classification
Evaluate reserve quality, liquidity and redemption resilience under stress
Assess systemic risk, bank exposures and supervisory tools for significant stablecoins
syllabus: Fiat-backed, asset-referenced, crypto-collateralised and algorithmic designs
Reserve composition, custody, attestation and redemption rights
Red flags: affiliated reserves, redemption frictions and unchecked policy changes
Runs, contagion and enhanced oversight of systemically significant stablecoins

modules.title: Cross-Border Cooperation, Enforcement and Crisis Management
modules.summary: Brings the programme together on the hardest cases: firms operating across borders, escalation to enforcement, and the failure of a crypto-asset firm, alongside the emerging risks supervisors must prepare for.
objectives: Operate cross-border cooperation and information exchange with other authorities
Apply the graduated enforcement toolkit proportionately with sound documentation
Manage a crypto firm in distress, drawing on lessons from major market failures
syllabus: Home-host responsibilities, supervisory colleges and regulatory arbitrage
From supervisory findings to enforcement: case files and rights of defence
Crisis management: early warning, client asset recovery and wind-down
Workshop: a cross-border crypto firm failure simulation

related.title: Crypto and Blockchain Fundamentals
related.summary: A ten-module foundation programme giving supervisors a practical understanding of blockchain, crypto-asset markets and service providers, and the risks they must supervise.

related.title: Digital Money: Stablecoins, Tokenised Deposits and CBDCs
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors and central bankers to assess stablecoins, tokenised deposits and CBDCs, and their risks to payments and financial stability.

related.title: MiCA Essentials for Supervisors (EU Edition)
related.summary: A six-module essentials programme giving EU national competent authority staff a practical command of MiCA, from token regimes and CASP authorisation to supervision and enforcement.

related.title: Supervising Crypto-Asset Service Providers under MiCA (EU Edition)
related.summary: An advanced fifteen-module programme equipping EU national competent authorities to authorise and supervise crypto-asset service providers and token issuers under MiCA.

related.title: Tokenisation of Financial Markets
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to assess tokenised securities, funds and collateral, DLT market infrastructure, settlement finality, custody and smart contract risk.

related.title: Quantum and Cryptographic Resilience
related.summary: A six-module programme equipping supervisors to assess firms' exposure to quantum threats, cryptographic inventories and post-quantum migration plans, and to set proportionate expectations.
